issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch for GroverLightsOutPuzzle: the template's class constructor requires an argument initial_state (def __init__(self, initial_state: list[int])) while the solution's constructor takes no arguments (def __init__(self)). The problem statement and the template's run() docstring/example show instantiation without passing initial_state (GroverLightsOutPuzzle()), so the template constructor signature is inconsistent with the intended usage and with the solution. This will confuse students and prevent running the provided run() example or following the solution structure.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template constructor signature consistent with the solution and problem examples. Either remove the initial_state parameter from the template's __init__ (def __init__(self):) so instantiation without arguments is valid, or update the template run() examples and documentation to show creating the class with an explicit initial_state argument (and propagate that parameter usage throughout). Prefer aligning the template to def __init__(self): (no parameter) to match the solution and example usage.

issues.description: Constructor API mismatch for the Lights Out puzzle class: the template declares GroverLightsOutPuzzle.__init__ with a parameter named initial_state (def __init__(self, initial_state: list[int])) while the solution implements GroverLightsOutPuzzle.__init__ with no such parameter (def __init__(self)). This inconsistent constructor signature represents the same conceptual entity (initial puzzle state / class initialization) with different identifiers/parameters across artifacts and can confuse students about how to instantiate and supply the puzzle initial state.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor/API consistent across artifacts. Either (A) remove the initial_state parameter from the template __init__ signature so both template and solution use def __init__(self), and accept the initial state only when calling grover_circuit (as in the solution), or (B) modify the solution to accept def __init__(self, initial_state: list[int]) and store/use that parameter consistently. Update the problem statement and examples to clearly show the chosen constructor usage.
